text:
Mariya (Support): FYI — ChroniclePay hitting 429s in prod across EU region since ~09:12 UTC. Customer says spikes are 'top-of-minute' but a bit noisy. They sent a few request/response snippets.

Mariya (Support): sample response headers from their client:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-RPM-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-RPM-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-TPM-Limit: 3000
X-RateLimit-TPM-Remaining: 10
Retry-After: 12
```

Mariya (Support): Notable: RPM shows 0 remaining but TPM still has capacity. Customer says their client fans out several short-lived connections per minute (serverless concurrency).

Jake (EngSRE): @Mariya can you paste a short curl we can use to repro? Also which tenant id and region?

Mariya (Support): tenant_id: chronicle-pay-prod, region: eu-central-1. Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer T.XXXX" \
  -d '{"input":"ping"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Mariya (Support): customer attached a short timeline: they do 6 concurrent lambda invocations each minute, each opens 3 HTTP/2 streams and does 4 short requests (30–120ms).

Lisa (Eng Runtime): sounds like per-minute bucketing alignment + multiplexing. If their bursts concentrate in the same second window we can hit RPM ceiling even with TPM headroom. :thinking:

Jake (EngSRE): Agree. Two quick checks: 1) confirm per-tenant RPM metrics on edge-batcher for chronicle-pay; 2) check connection/stream concurrency signals in the proxy (http2_streams_active). Can someone grab edge metrics for last 15m?

infra-bot: alert: tenant chronicle-pay-prod has had 87 429 responses in the last 10 minutes (eu-central-1). Trigger: tenant_ratecap_spike.

Jake (EngSRE): I pulled metrics — RPM rolling window (60s) spiking to 140 at 09:12 while configured RPM limit is 120. TPM steady at ~2k. Request distribution is concentrated around the minute boundary.

Vikas (CSM): Customer is on the Growth plan — we can offer a temporary RPM uplift if they need an immediate fix while they change client behavior. They asked for guidance first.

Jake (EngSRE): Recommended immediate mitigations (short term):
- Advise customer to jitter their lambda cron/randomize start times across a 60s window.
- If they can't, we can apply a short-lived RPM bump for a day while they roll out changes.
- On our side, enable tenant-level smoothing for the edge-batcher (turn on 10s window smoothing) to spread spikes.

Lisa (Eng Runtime): Long-term: suggest we add a client advisory doc: "Avoid tight minute-aligned fanout; use jitter/backoff; prefer persistent connections and fewer concurrent streams." Also add a prescriptive SDK snippet.

Jake (EngSRE): For debugging, request the customer enable verbose client telemetry for 5 minutes and return the following log lines:
```
[ts] tenant=chronicle-pay-prod conn_id=... http2_streams=... request_ms=... status=...
```

Mariya (Support): I sent mitigation steps + suggested curl for telemetry to customer. They asked for a sample retry/backoff snippet they can drop into lambdas. I posted one below.

Mariya (Support): client backoff snippet suggestion (JS):
```
// exponential backoff with jitter
async function callWithBackoff(fn, tries=5){
  for(let i=0;i<tries;i++){
    try { return await fn(); } catch(e){
      const base = Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2,i), 10000);
      const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random()*200);
      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, base + jitter));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries exceeded');
}
```

Lisa (Eng Runtime): Also include guidance to reuse a single HTTP/2 connection per lambda invocation (keepalive) and limit concurrent streams to ~4 if possible. That reduces per-connection burstiness.

Jake (EngSRE): Operational notes for triage team:
- Confirm we don't have an unrelated routing issue (there's none in region now).
- If customer supplies telemetry showing minute-boundary clustering, approve temporary RPM bump (via billing/ops) and schedule follow-up to roll back after 24h.
- If churn continues after client changes, consider automating minute-smoothed quota enforcement.

Vikas (CSM): I'll coordinate a one-hour call with ChroniclePay and ask them to enable telemetry and apply lambda jitter. I'll also propose the short RPM uplift if they need it right away.

Mariya (Support): Customer replied: "We can enable jitter and telemetry now. Please do the temporary uplift while we roll forward." They requested ETA for uplift.

Jake (EngSRE): I can approve a 24h RPM uplift from 120->180 for the tenant. @ops please implement and notify when live.

infra-bot: ops action: rpm-uplift applied for tenant chronicle-pay-prod (120->180) — effective immediately. Ticket: OPS-4521.

Mariya (Support): Customer confirmed 429s dropped to near-zero after uplift and jitter rollout. They will keep telemetry on for 6h and report.

Lisa (Eng Runtime): Follow-up items: add a short KB on "minute-boundary fanout" to support docs, add a test case in edge-batcher e2e to validate smoothing window behavior, and consider exposing a per-tenant recommended concurrency field in Console.

Jake (EngSRE): Closing loop: note in ticket OPS-4521 that uplift was timeboxed to 24h and customer will roll client changes. If telemetry shows persistent issues after rollback, escalate. :thumbsup:

Mariya (Support): Thanks all — keeping this thread pinned to the ticket.
